newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends steady, market short heading to CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends steady, market short heading to CPI.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed steady in busy trade on Thursday on the eve of key December quarter inflation data.

The currency finished at US$0.7036/43 and 68.08 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7039/46 and 68.18 at the opening. "The market in general, especially from New York, have positioned themselves to go short in the lead-up to it and I think the market's taken it on itself to look to a very low CPI," said a Wellington dealer.

But he said the currency and TWI were at fair levels considering how far short-term rates had fallen in recent weeks. Only if quarterly underlying inflation came in substantially below the Reserve Bank's forecast of 0.5 percent was the bank likely to sanction a further easing.

"Frankly, if they do, it won't be below seven percent anyway, in which case these people who've positioned themselves short are probably going to get a horrible shock -- the currency's not in fact going to go down substantially," he said. Ninety-day bills closed at 7.43 percent.

While a low CPI would take rates and the the Kiwi lower, a number in line with Reserve Bank expectations or higher had potential to push the currency higher. There were euro issues to be settled and, with the meat season in progress, plenty of exporter business to be done, the dealer said.
Another said the currency had an underlying bid tone thanks to local exporter buying, but with options-related offers in the 0.7045 area.
The Kiwi had bounced from firm support overnight at 0.7010-15, and traded a 0.7030-47 range on the day. CPI data are due at 2145 GMT Friday. -- Mark Trevelyan 64 4 471-4277
